lessons.0.slides.1.title: Import Procedure Overview
lessons.0.slides.1.content: Wine import is a complex international trade process involving: domaine purchasing, freight transport, customs clearance, inspection and quarantine, tax processing, warehousing, and distribution. The time required is typically 2–3 months (sea freight) or 1–2 weeks (air freight). Costs include: wine cost, freight, insurance, customs duties, VAT, inspection fees, and storage fees.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 📦 Complete Procedure Steps
lessons.0.slides.2.points.0: Step 1: Place order with domaine — confirm allocation, price, and delivery date
lessons.0.slides.2.points.1: Step 2: Sign contract — purchase agreement, payment terms
lessons.0.slides.2.points.2: Step 3: Obtain documents — certificate of origin, health certificate, invoice
lessons.0.slides.2.points.3: Step 4: Arrange transport — select freight forwarder, temperature-controlled shipping
lessons.0.slides.2.points.4: Step 5: Customs declaration — HS code, import permit
lessons.0.slides.2.points.5: Step 6: Pay duties and taxes — customs duties, VAT, excise tax
lessons.0.slides.2.points.6: Step 7: Inspection and quarantine — comply with importing country standards
lessons.0.slides.2.points.7: Step 8: Collect and warehouse — temperature-controlled storage management
lessons.0.slides.3.title: Choosing Transport Mode
lessons.0.slides.3.content: Sea freight is the mainstream (low cost, suitable for large volumes) but takes 2–3 months; temperature control is a challenge. Air freight is fast (1–2 weeks) but costs 3–5× more — suitable for high-value wines or urgent needs. Land transport (within Europe) is economical. Cold-chain shipping is critical, especially in summer, requiring full temperature control (12–16°C) throughout.

lessons.1.slides.1.title: 💰 Main Tax Structure
lessons.1.slides.1.points.0: Customs duty — varies by importing country (China 14%, Taiwan 10%, Hong Kong 0%)
lessons.1.slides.1.points.2: Excise tax — levied in some countries (China 10%)
lessons.1.slides.1.points.4: Other costs — brokerage fees, storage fees
lessons.1.slides.2.title: Tax Rate Comparison Across Markets
lessons.1.slides.3.title: Tax Optimisation Strategies
lessons.1.slides.3.content: Legal tax planning options include: (1) leveraging free-trade zone policies (e.g., Shanghai FTZ); (2) bonded warehousing (deferred tax); (3) reasonable declared value (must reflect market fair value); (4) bulk imports to reduce per-unit cost; (5) leveraging FTAs such as RCEP. Warning: avoid illegal practices such as undervaluing — the consequences are severe.
lessons.1.slides.4.title: 💰 Burgundy Wine Import Cost Structure (China Market Example — €50 Wine)
lessons.1.slides.4.content: Combined customs and tax burden reaching 48% is the biggest cost. After adding logistics, storage, and margin, a €50 wine retails in China for €135–150. Hong Kong's 0% tariff is a natural advantage.

lessons.2.title: Logistics and Temperature Control Management
lessons.2.slides.0.title: Logistics and Temperature Control Management
lessons.2.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 3 - 15 min
lessons.2.slides.1.title: The Critical Importance of Temperature Control
lessons.2.slides.1.content: Burgundy wines are extremely sensitive to temperature. Exceeding 25°C during transit causes 'cooked wine' (Cooked Wine) — irreversible damage to quality. Ideal transport temperature: 12–16°C, avoiding sharp fluctuations. Summer shipments require refrigerated containers (Reefer Containers), increasing costs by 30–50% but essential. Top wines should be temperature-controlled throughout — trucks, warehouses, and last-mile delivery.
lessons.2.slides.2.title: 🌡️ Key Temperature-Control Checkpoints
lessons.2.slides.2.points.1: Transit — refrigerated container or air freight temperature control
lessons.2.slides.2.points.2: Port / airport — fast customs clearance, avoid sun exposure
lessons.2.slides.2.points.5: Monitoring records — temperature logger tracking throughout

lessons.3.slides.2.title: Exhibition Strategies
lessons.3.slides.2.content: Reasons for attending include: building domaine relationships, finding new suppliers, observing market trends, competitor analysis, and networking. Preparation: pre-schedule domaine meetings, bring business cards and materials, understand the product range, prepare budget, and sharpen tasting skills. Follow-up is crucial — 80% of business opportunities come from post-fair follow-up.

lessons.4.slides.0.title: En Primeur Futures Trading
lessons.4.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 5 - 14 min
lessons.4.slides.1.title: What Is En Primeur?
lessons.4.slides.1.content: En Primeur (futures) means purchasing wine before it is bottled — typically ordering after tasting barrel samples 6–12 months after harvest, with delivery 2–3 years later. Advantages: lower price (usually 20–30% below release price), guaranteed allocation (for sought-after wines), investment opportunity. Risks: price decline, quality falls short of expectations, domaine ceases to exist. The Burgundy En Primeur market is less mature than Bordeaux's, but top domaines also offer this mechanism.
